findings.claim: Carry from nit-SAFE-R2-001 (NO ACTION disposition from R2 confirmed). The sanitisation filter at generate-scorecard-report.py lines 160–164 passes through Unicode C1 control codes (U+0080–U+009F) via the condition ord(c) >= 0x20. Fix-round-2 did not touch this filter; the NO ACTION disposition stands.
findings.evidence: generate-scorecard-report.py lines 160–164: sanitised = ''.join(' ' if c in ('\n', '\r') else c for c in raw_error if c == '\t' or ord(c) >= 0x20)[:1500]. The condition ord(c) >= 0x20 admits all code points U+0020 and above, including the C1 control block U+0080–U+009F. The sanitised string is consumed at line 167 as the body of a single-line markdown blockquote (> {sanitised}). The CR/LF replacement guarantees no embedded newlines reach the blockquote prefix, eliminating multiline injection. Source of raw_error is index.get('error') from a CODEOWNERS-protected index.json; hostile content requires write access to the output/scorecards/** protected tree.
findings.impact: Negligible. C1 control codes produce no visible output and no structural effect in browser-rendered markdown or GitHub PR diff views. The single-line blockquote constraint prevents multiline injection regardless of C1 passthrough. No policy-enforcement bypass, no data exfiltration, no safety invariant regression.
findings.mitigation: NO ACTION for this slice. Optional future defence-in-depth: replace ord(c) >= 0x20 with (0x20 <= ord(c) <= 0x7E) or ord(c) >= 0xA0 to strip C1 controls while preserving printable ASCII and non-control Unicode. Defer to a future cleanup slice; do not block merge.

findings.claim: The schema_version mismatch error in generate-scorecard-report.py main() uses the same GitHub Actions annotation code SCP-E001 as the file-not-found error. The R2 mitigation for MAJ-SAFE-R2-001 explicitly proposed SCP-E002 for the schema mismatch condition. Two distinct failure modes now share one error code, making programmatic error-routing by CI annotation parsers ambiguous.
findings.evidence: generate-scorecard-report.py line 199: print(f'::error file={args.index},title=SCP-E001::scorecard index not found', file=sys.stderr) — file-not-found path. Line 212: f'::error file={args.index},title=SCP-E001::unsupported scorecard-index schema_version {schema_version!r}; ...' — schema mismatch path. Both use title=SCP-E001. The R2 mitigation (review-safety-r2.json, MAJ-SAFE-R2-001 mitigation field) specified title=SCP-E002 for the schema mismatch. By contrast, tools.py line 329 correctly uses a distinct error_code='SCP-MCP-SCORECARD-004' for the MCP-side schema_version error.
findings.impact: No safety impact. The message text clearly differentiates the two conditions; both paths exit 1 and the guard correctly rejects unsupported schema_version values regardless of the annotation code. A CI system parsing annotation titles to route alerts would mis-classify the schema mismatch failure as a file-not-found failure, potentially routing to the wrong oncall owner or suppression rule.
findings.mitigation: In generate-scorecard-report.py line 212, change title=SCP-E001 to title=SCP-E002 to match the R2 mitigation spec and differentiate the schema mismatch condition from the file-not-found condition. No test changes required; the guard behaviour (exit 1) is unchanged. Does not block merge.
